items.title: Tell your care team about low readings
items.text: 5.5% of your readings were below 70 mg/dL (weeks 11-12); the usual target is under 4%. Low sugar can make you shaky or dizzy. Contact your care team today rather than waiting for your next visit.

rejected.text: If your sugar readings are below 70 mg/dL, you might feel shaky or dizzy, so contact your care team today. Your care team can help you with readings that are below the usual target of under 4%.

items.title: Take a short walk after meals
items.text: Your sugar rose about 23.7 mg/dL less after meals when you walked. Aim for 10 to 20 minutes after dinner, where the program saw the biggest gain (18.3 mg/dL). A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a fifth of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet. Because of your low readings, check with your care team before walking more. Walk after eating, not on an empty stomach, carry juice or glucose tablets, and stop to check your sugar if you feel shaky, sweaty or confused.

rejected.text: Walking after meals can help with your sugar, which rose about 23.7 mg/dL less when you walked. Try walking 10 to 20 minutes after dinner, but check with your care team first because of your low readings.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: Having dinner at 8 pm or later, like you do 75.0% of the time, is linked to sugar rising more after meals. Try to start dinner before 8 pm, as sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners than after earlier ones.

items.title: Hold off on longer fasts for now
items.text: 5.5% of your readings were below 70 mg/dL, so check with your care team before stretching your overnight fast. Right now it averages 12.5 hours.

rejected.text: Your overnight fast currently averages 12.5 hours, but check with your care team before making any changes. If 5.5% of your readings are below 70 mg/dL, your care team can help you decide what to do about your overnight fast.
